questions.text: Staff Digital Skills & Training: Ability to operate systems: (1) Computer literacy of frontline staff; (2) Training on specific ID software; (3) Troubleshooting basic issues; (4) Data privacy training (handling personal data); (5) Customer service skills (digital assistance); (6) Change management support; (7) Certification requirements.
questions.evidence_required: Training logs, Skill assessment results, User feedback
questions.africa_specific_notes: Frontline staff often resist digital tools due to lack of training or fear of job loss. 'System is down' is often code for 'I don't know how to use it'.

questions.text: Technical Leadership (CIO/CTO): Strategic capacity: (1) Presence of CIOs in ministries; (2) Technical understanding of leadership; (3) Ability to manage vendors; (4) Strategic planning for IT; (5) Innovation culture; (6) Data-driven decision making; (7) Retention of tech talent.
questions.evidence_required: Org chart (CIO role), IT strategy docs, Vendor performance reviews
questions.africa_specific_notes: Government struggles to retain tech talent against private sector salaries. Leadership often non-technical.

questions.text: Large-Scale Project Management: Delivering on time: (1) Project management methodology (Prince2/Agile?); (2) Track record of delivery; (3) Risk management capacity; (4) Stakeholder engagement skills; (5) Budget management; (6) Pilot testing rigor; (7) Post-implementation review.
questions.evidence_required: Project plans, Risk registers, Progress reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: GovTech projects notorious for delays and failure. 'Big Bang' launches often fail; iterative approach needed.

questions.text: Vendor Management & Negotiation: Getting value: (1) Contract negotiation skills; (2) SLA monitoring capacity; (3) Avoiding vendor capture; (4) Technical audit of deliverables; (5) Dispute resolution skills; (6) Knowledge transfer enforcement; (7) Cost benchmarking.
questions.evidence_required: Contract review minutes, SLA reports, Vendor audits
questions.africa_specific_notes: Governments often out-negotiated by global tech giants. Capacity to enforce contracts is weak.

questions.text: Assisted Digital Services: Helping the offline: (1) Availability of 'Huduma Centers' (one-stop shops); (2) Agent network for government services; (3) Staff ability to assist low-literacy users; (4) Proxy transaction protocols (can I do it for my grandma?); (5) Paper alternatives availability; (6) Outreach to remote areas; (7) Cost of assistance.
questions.evidence_required: Center locations map, Agent training manuals, Transaction logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digital-only services exclude millions. 'Intermediaries' (agents/cyber cafes) are the bridge.

questions.text: User Experience (UX) Design: Usability for all: (1) Mobile-first design; (2) Low-bandwidth optimization; (3) Local language interfaces; (4) Accessibility features (voice/text); (5) User testing with diverse groups; (6) Feedback loops; (7) Simplicity of forms.
questions.evidence_required: UX audit, User testing reports, Interface screenshots
questions.africa_specific_notes: Gov portals often complex and desktop-only. Must work on a $30 smartphone on 2G.

questions.text: Cyber Defense Capabilities: Protecting the realm: (1) CERT/CIRT (Computer Emergency Response Team) capacity; (2) Threat intelligence sharing; (3) Incident response drills; (4) Forensic capabilities; (5) Ethical hacking program; (6) Staff awareness training; (7) Partnership with private sector security.
questions.evidence_required: Drill reports, Threat intel feeds, Staff certifications
questions.africa_specific_notes: State-sponsored attacks increasing. National CERTs need resources and authority.

questions.text: Data Analytics & Policy Making: Evidence-based policy: (1) Ability to analyze ID data for planning; (2) Privacy-preserving analytics (differential privacy); (3) Data visualization skills; (4) Sharing insights across ministries; (5) Data quality management; (6) Ethics of data use; (7) Open data publication skills.
questions.evidence_required: Policy papers using data, Dashboards, Data sharing protocols
questions.africa_specific_notes: Data often sits in silos. Using ID data to plan schools/hospitals is the ultimate dividend.

scoring_notes: Layer 4 (Competence) for Government in SSA: It's not just about buying software; it's about the people. Civil service capacity and citizen support are the bottlenecks.
